scope.flow: TokenWrapper.transferFrom emits a Transfer event with the wrong from field
evidence: `TokenWrapper.transferFrom` emits a non-standard `Transfer` event (`msg.sender` instead of `from`)
`ERC-20` mandates that the `Transfer` event always identify the token holder whose balance decreases in the `from` field
But in `TokenWrapper.sol` the `transferFrom` implementation emits the spender (`msg.sender`) as `from`, rather than the approved token owner (`from` parameter).

statements.text: A spender calls TokenWrapper.transferFrom, supplying an approved token owner as the from parameter.
evidence: But in `TokenWrapper.sol` the `transferFrom` implementation emits the spender (`msg.sender`) as `from`, rather than the approved token owner (`from` parameter).

statements.text: The Transfer event emitted by transferFrom must identify in its from field the token holder whose balance decreases (the approved token owner), not the spender.
evidence: `ERC-20` mandates that the `Transfer` event always identify the token holder whose balance decreases in the `from` field
But in `TokenWrapper.sol` the `transferFrom` implementation emits the spender (`msg.sender`) as `from`, rather than the approved token owner (`from` parameter).

statements.text: TokenWrapper.transferFrom emits the spender (msg.sender) as the from field of the Transfer event instead of the approved token owner (from parameter).

statements.text: ERC-20 non-compliance – automated tooling may treat the token as invalid or malfunction when reconstructing balances from events.
evidence: ERC-20 non-compliance – automated tooling may treat the token as invalid or malfunction when reconstructing balances from events.

statements.text: Incorrect attribution – wallets, indexers, subgraphs, analytics and airdrop scripts will record the spender as the debited account, corrupting historical data, balances, and accounting.
evidence: Incorrect attribution – wallets, indexers, subgraphs, analytics and airdrop scripts will record the spender as the debited account, corrupting historical data, balances, and accounting.

statements.text: Operational risk – once deployed, the incorrect events are immutable; integrators must add special-case logic or accept corrupted data.
